# [Week THIRTEEN]{.r-fit-text}

# Demoing Static Visual Design

## Robert Johnson Page
This is a two part exercise.

1. Create a style sheet
2. Use the style sheet to create an actual webpage about the song "Hellhound on my Trail" by Robert Johnson

## Style sheet
The style sheet can be a png, a pdf, or a jpg file containing the following elements.

1. A color palette with about four or five colors
2. A type guide, with at least two typefaces in several sizes
3. A layout guide, such as a grid

## Using the style sheet
1. Create an actual webpage, not a Figjam
2. Display the following information
   a. A picture of your choice
   b. The lyrics to "Hellhound on my Trail" (recorded 1937)
   c. Some biographical information about Robert Johnson (1911--1938)

## Turning it in
In the Robert Johnson Page assignment box, provide the stylesheet and a link to the webpage. If you don't have a place to host the webpage, put all the assets (the html file, a css file, and the picture file) in the assignment box so that they display there.

# Demoing dynamic visual design

## Superstore Visualization
This is a four part exercise.

1. Specify a graphic using Bertin's system
2. Have an AI generate an R script from your specification
3. Critique the result against your specification
4. Revise

## The assistant
Last week you pretended to give a table and a sketch to an assistant to polish. This week the assistant is an AI. It will write an R script using ggplot2, a package built on the ideas of Bertin and of @Wilkinson2005, whom we meet next week.

::: {.notes}
The point of the exercise is the specification and the critique, not the chart. The AI will produce a plausible chart from almost any prompt. The question is whether it is the chart you specified and whether it answers your question at a glance.
:::

## The data
Global Superstore is an Excel spreadsheet recording orders, returns, and people for a fictional store operating worldwide. We will use only the Orders worksheet, where each row is one line of an order.

## Get the data
Download the spreadsheet from Canvas > Files > visualization > `GlobalSuperstore.xls`

## Set up Posit Cloud
Posit Cloud runs R and RStudio in your browser, so there is nothing to install.

1. Go to [https://posit.cloud](https://posit.cloud)
2. Sign up for the free plan
3. In Your Workspace, click New Project, then New RStudio Project
4. Give the project a name, such as superstore

## Upload the data
1. Find the Files pane in the lower right of RStudio
2. Click Upload
3. Click Choose File and select `GlobalSuperstore.xls`
4. Click OK and wait for the file to appear in the Files pane

## Read the data {.scale85}
Type the following in the Console pane, one line at a time. The first line may take a few minutes and you only need to run it once.

```r
if (!require("pacman")) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}
pacman::p_load(tidyverse,readxl)
orders <- read_excel("GlobalSuperstore.xls", sheet = "Orders")
```

## Look at the columns
`glimpse(orders)` lists every column, its type, and its first few values. You can also type `View(orders)` to browse the rows.

## {.center}
Stop here. We will look at the columns together.

::: {.notes}
Pause to show the columns in Posit Cloud. Point out the kinds of columns: dates (Order Date, Ship Date), places (City, State, Country, Region, Market), categories (Segment, Category, Sub-Category, Ship Mode, Order Priority), and quantities (Sales, Quantity, Discount, Profit, Shipping Cost). Each kind suggests a level: nominal, ordered, or quantitative.
:::

## Part 1: Specify
Do this part without AI.

1. Choose a question the Orders data can answer
2. Write the invariant as a one-line title
3. List the components
4. Match each component to a variable
5. Sketch the graphic

## The invariant
The invariant is the topic of the graphic and gives the graphic its title, for instance *Profit by market and product category*.

## The components
For each component, give

- its order (raw or fraction)
- its length (number of divisions)
- its level (nominal, ordered, or quantitative)

## The variables
Name what will carry each component: one of the two dimensions of the plane, or a retinal variable (size, value, texture, color, orientation, or shape).

## The sketch
Sketch the graphic on paper or on a tablet. Include the title, the axes, and a legend for each component.

## Part 2: Generate
Give an AI of your choice

1. Your specification
2. The output of `glimpse(orders)`, pasted from the Console, so that the AI knows the column names
3. A request for an R script using ggplot2 that reads the Orders worksheet of `GlobalSuperstore.xls`

Keep a log of every prompt you write.

## Save your prompt log
The log is a document listing every prompt you wrote, in order. Save it in one of these ways.

1. Keep a document open and paste each prompt into it as you send it
2. When you finish, scroll back through the chat and copy each of your prompts into a document
3. If your AI offers a share link to the chat, add the link to the document as well

Include prompts that failed. Do not edit them.

## Run the script
1. In RStudio, click File, then New File, then R Script
2. Paste the script and save it as `superstore.R`
3. Click Source to run it
4. If you see an error, paste the error message back to the AI

## Part 3: Critique
Compare the chart to your specification and your sketch.

- Where did the AI depart from your specification?
- What did the AI choose that you did not ask for, such as a color scale, a sort order, or an axis range?
- Does each component have a legend?
- Does the chart answer your question at a glance?

## Part 4: Revise
Prompt the AI at least once more to repair what you found in the critique. Note what you changed and why.

## Save the chart {.scale85}
Add this line to the end of the script and run the script again.

```r
ggsave("superstore.png", width = 8, height = 5)
```

To download a file from Posit Cloud, check its box in the Files pane, click More, then Export.

## Turning it in
In the Superstore Visualization assignment box, provide the following.

1. Your specification: invariant, components, variables, and sketch
2. Your prompt log
3. The final R script and the final chart
4. Your critique, including what you revised and why
